relevance_rank_note: Directly about apoE held on the cell surface by the LDL receptor and about remnant internalisation being delayed as a result, which is the mechanism H4 describes, but almost every quantified comparison is apoE2 versus apoE4 or LDL receptor level within apoE4; where apoE3 appears it is grouped with apoE4 or graded only qualitatively, so the apoE4-versus-apoE3 contrast this hypothesis needs is carried by one qualitative imaging grading and two nulls, with no binding measured and no receptor recycling or surface level measured.

description: Immunostaining of liver sections for human apoE compared mice carrying the high-expressing human LDL receptor minigene on an apoE4 versus an apoE3 background: both showed apoE drawn to the sinusoidal front where the receptor sits, but the sinusoidal signal relative to cytoplasmic signal was less intense with apoE3 than with apoE4, which the authors read as the receptor level influencing sinusoidal localisation of apoE4 and, to a lesser extent, apoE3.
quote: except that the sinusoidal staining relative to cytoplasmic staining was less intense in the Apoe3/3Ldlrh/+ liver than in the Apoe4/4Ldlrh/+ liver. This suggests that the LDLR levels influence sinusoidal localization of apoE4 and, to a lesser extent, of apoE3.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (more apoE held at the LDLR-bearing sinusoidal hepatocyte surface)
system: Liver paraffin sections (5 micron) from mice homozygous for replacement of the mouse apoE gene with human APOE*3 or APOE*4 and carrying the human LDL receptor minigene allele Ldlrh/+ giving 2- to 3-fold normal LDL receptor expression, backcrossed at least 6 generations to C57BL/6 and fed a high-fat Western diet (21% fat, 0.2% cholesterol) for at least 2 weeks; immunohistochemistry with antibody against human apoE, 600x, compared with anti-human LDL receptor staining on matched sections. Mouse liver in vivo, not human brain cells; the readout is apoE immunostaining intensity at the sinusoidal surface, not a measurement of apoE binding to the receptor and not a measurement of receptor recycling or receptor surface level.
human_check: No figure image was viewed; the apoE4-versus-apoE3 grading is taken from the Results sentence quoted, not read off the micrographs. The comparison is a qualitative staining-intensity judgement by the authors with no quantification, no statistics and no stated number of mice or sections for Figure 2, hence qualitative / visual_only and N/A for both P and n. ApoE4 is only colocalised with the LDL receptor in the sense that the intense staining sits on sinusoids where anti-human-LDL-receptor staining is also seen on matched sections (Fig 2A-2B); no co-immunoprecipitation or affinity measurement is made, so this is class 3, not class 1. The row depends on the high-LDL-receptor background being present in both arms, so it is an apoE4-versus-apoE3 comparison at matched receptor level rather than a receptor manipulation. The human should decide whether an author-stated relative intensity with no quantification is worth keeping at all.

description: Confocal imaging of livers from apoE-deficient mice given adenoviral apoE4-GFP, apoE3-GFP or apoE2-GFP, with or without the high human LDL receptor background, found that apoE4-GFP and apoE3-GFP both accumulated subendothelially on the hepatocyte surface in the space of Disse and both were more pronounced when the receptor was high, whereas apoE2-GFP barely accumulated; apoE4 and apoE3 are reported together with no difference drawn between them, so this panel is an apoE4-versus-apoE3 null and the isoform separation it shows is apoE2 against the other two.
quote: The subendothelial accumulation of apoE4-GFP or apoE3-GFP was more pronounced in the liver of the Apoe−/−Ldlrh/h mice injected with Ad-apoE4-GFP or Ad-apoE3-GFP (Figure 3A and 3B). In marked contrast, Ad-apoE2-GFP showed little accumulation of apoE2-GFP on the hepatocyte surface even in the Apoe−/−Ldlrh/h mice (Figure 3C).
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no stated difference in apoE accumulation on the hepatocyte surface; both exceed APOE2)
system: ApoE-deficient mice (Apoe-/-) and Apoe-/-Ldlrh/h mice homozygous for the high-expressing human LDL receptor minigene, backcrossed at least 6 generations to C57BL/6 and fed a high-fat Western diet for at least 2 weeks, injected via tail vein with 1x10^9 PFU adenovirus encoding apoE2-GFP, apoE3-GFP or apoE4-GFP (EGFP fused to the apoE C terminus); livers perfusion-fixed 5 days later, 100 micron vibratome sections stained with Alexafluor633-labelled lectin to mark sinusoids and the space of Disse, confocal microscopy at 600x. Mouse liver in vivo with virally expressed GFP-tagged human apoE, not human brain cells; the readout is fluorescence localisation, not apoE-receptor binding and not receptor recycling or surface level.
human_check: No figure image was viewed; the apoE4 and apoE3 panels are reported in one clause and the text states no difference between them, so this is recorded as against: true (an apoE4-versus-apoE3 null) rather than as support. The human should note this is an absence of a stated difference, not a tested null: the paper draws no statistical comparison here, gives no quantification and states no number of mice per group for Figure 3, hence qualitative / visual_only and N/A for P and n. If a figure image were viewed the two panels might show a visible difference the text does not mention, which would change the direction of this row; that is the main thing to check. Note also the caveat the authors raise themselves, that the apoE-GFP on the surface may be derived from apoE-GFP secreted by other transfected hepatocytes rather than by the cell it sits on, and that the tag is a C-terminal EGFP fusion.

description: Western blot quantification of apoE in the medium relative to cell-associated apoE in primary hepatocytes cultured 24 h without serum put apoE2 cells at twice the ratio of apoE3 or apoE4 cells, with apoE3 and apoE4 reported as the same value: the isoform grading of apoE held inside the cell rather than released tracks the low-affinity apoE2 against the other two and gives no apoE4-versus-apoE3 difference.
quote: The ratio of medium apoE to cell-associated apoE in the Apoe2/2 cells was twice as high as those of Apoe3/3 or Apoe4/4 cells (Figure 1C).
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no difference in the secreted-to-cell-associated apoE ratio; both below APOE2)
system: Primary hepatocytes isolated from mice homozygous for replacement of the mouse apoE gene with human APOE*2, APOE*3 or APOE*4, backcrossed at least 6 generations to C57BL/6 and fed a high-fat Western diet (21% fat, 0.2% cholesterol) for at least 2 weeks; cells plated on mouse collagen IV-coated dishes and cultured in DMEM without FBS for 24 h, then apoE in medium and in cell lysate measured by Western blot and expressed as a ratio; average of 3 wells, 1-way ANOVA with Tukey-Kramer honestly significant difference. Mouse primary hepatocytes with endogenously expressed human apoE isoforms, not human brain cells; the readout is a steady-state secretion-to-retention ratio, not apoE binding to the receptor and not receptor recycling or receptor surface level.
human_check: No figure image was viewed. The printed 2-fold is the apoE2-versus-apoE3-or-apoE4 ratio, not an apoE4-versus-apoE3 magnitude, so it is not placed in the effect column and the row is recorded as an apoE4-versus-apoE3 null, against: true. The Figure 1 legend gives **P<=0.005 and ***P<=0.0005 without saying which panel or which pair of bars carries which star, so p is N/A / ambiguous_panel; a figure image would be needed to see whether any bracket sits on the apoE3-versus-apoE4 pair, and none was viewed. n = 3 wells is from the Figure 1 legend statement that values are the average of 3 wells, and the legend adds that the experiment was repeated once with a similar result. This is a null by omission: the text groups apoE3 and apoE4 at one value rather than reporting a test between them.

description: Clearance of DiI-labelled apoE-free VLDL from plasma after tail-vein injection was compared across isoform backgrounds all carrying the high human LDL receptor allele: apoE3 and apoE4 mice did not differ from each other at 10 minutes, and over the following 10 minutes the VLDL was removed significantly faster in the apoE2 mice than in both the apoE3 and the apoE4 mice, so the delayed internalisation the paper attributes to high apoE-receptor affinity separates apoE2 from the other two isoforms but does not separate apoE4 from apoE3.
quote: The clearance in the Apoe2/2Ldlrh/+, Apoe3/3Ldlrh/+, and Apoe4/4Ldlrh/+ mice were not different at 10 minutes after injection. However, the VLDL was removed from circulation during the next 10 minutes significantly faster in the Apoe2/2Ldlrh/+ mice than in both Apoe3/3Ldlrh/+ and Apoe4/4Ldlrh/+mice.
summary: (APOE3 -> APOE4) -> (no difference in plasma clearance of injected VLDL remnants)
system: Mice homozygous for human APOE*2, APOE*3 or APOE*4 replacement of the mouse apoE gene carrying the human LDL receptor minigene allele Ldlrh/+ (2- to 3-fold normal LDL receptor), backcrossed at least 6 generations to C57BL/6 and fed a high-fat Western diet for at least 2 weeks; VLDL isolated from pooled Apoe-/- plasma at d < 1.006 g/mL, DiI-labelled, 100 micrograms protein injected into the tail vein, plasma fluorescence read by microscope fluorometer at 2, 10 and 20 minutes with the 2-minute value as 100%, n = 4; 1-way ANOVA with Tukey-Kramer honestly significant difference. Mouse whole-animal plasma clearance in vivo, not human brain cells; the readout is disappearance of a labelled lipoprotein from plasma, not apoE-receptor binding and not receptor recycling or surface level.
human_check: No figure image was viewed. The apoE4-versus-apoE3 comparison is a stated no-difference at 10 minutes and, in the 10-to-20-minute window, the paper reports only that apoE2 was faster than both of the other two, so the apoE4-versus-apoE3 contrast is a null and is recorded as against: true. No numeric P and no magnitude is printed for any comparison in this panel, and the Figure 4 legend carries no star key, so eff is qualitative / visual_only and p is N/A / not_found_in_source; the significance statement in the text is for the apoE2 contrast, not for apoE4 versus apoE3, and must not be borrowed for this row. n = 4 is printed in the Figure 4A legend and is the number of mice; the human should confirm it applies to every genotype arm and not only to one. The human may also judge this row too far from H4 to keep, since plasma clearance is two steps removed from receptor adhesion; it is included because the paper's central claim is that apoE4's receptor affinity delays internalisation, and this is the one place that claim is tested with an apoE3 arm present.
